source.data_source: Armaly, Durst, Pereira & Schoenung, J. Fluid Mech. 127:473 (1983). Laminar 2D backward-facing step, expansion ratio 1.94. Primary recirculation reattachment length xr/S on the bottom wall vs Re (based on 2x step height and mean inlet velocity). At Re=389 the flow is in the steady two-dimensional laminar regime; Armaly's measured/computed primary reattachment is xr/S ~ 8 in this Re range.
source.ref_data_source: Armaly et al. 1983 J. Fluid Mech. 127:473-496, primary reattachment x1/S vs Re (their figure 2 / table). Re=389 sits in the steady 2D laminar branch where 2D simulation matches the experiment well.
source.note: gt_value is this repo's own OpenFOAM oracle at the case's own grid level, NOT Armaly. It was originally written by tools/autocal_kpis.py from a run nobody recorded (calibration_date said 'auto'), and the contract was rewritten after that run (#29), so the number was unprovenanced until it was re-measured under issue #119 — see oracle_provenance. The Armaly anchor (xr/S ~ 8 at this Re) is the magnitude check the value passes, not its source.
source.of_signconv_note: Cf = -2 tau_x / U_ref^2 (negate raw OpenFOAM wallShearStress.x): positive=attached, negative=recirc. Reattachment detector takes the first negative->positive Cf zero crossing past x/S=0.5 (filters spurious step-corner flickers).

reattachment_length_xr_over_h.description: Primary recirculation reattachment length on the bottom wall, xr/S, from the negative->positive Cf (wall-shear sign) crossing downstream of the step (x_min=0.5 S filter excludes step-corner artifacts; x_max=30 S)
reattachment_length_xr_over_h.pass_tol_source: Flat 5% of |gt_value| — the single band every live track carries (#190, after #188 set it for combustion and battery). The band exists to catch a wrong configuration, not to grade numerical precision, and scoring inside it is binary. Unchanged in value — this case already carried 5%. The band's floor is the measured grid-family spread in oracle_provenance.variants: quartering the cell count moves xr/S by 0.64%, so 5% sits well above what mesh choice alone can produce and the band is not scoring noise. The oracle lands on gt_value. physics_min = 3 / physics_max = 15 bracket the laminar steady-regime reattachment for ER ~ 1.94.
reattachment_length_xr_over_h.kpi_quality_note: ANTI-SHORTCUT STATUS: STRONG. The reattachment length of a laminar separating/reattaching shear layer has NO closed-form solution — it is set by the laminar separation dynamics and is the canonical Armaly experimental/CFD validation quantity. It cannot be inferred from flat-plate or boundary-layer correlations. Under this track's contract the scored number is not the one the agent writes: the evaluator deletes results.csv along with every generated artefact and re-runs the submission's own Allrun, so a recalled 'about 8' cannot score unless the submitted case actually computes it — which is what keeps acceptance.md's second falsifiable check satisfied even though the literature's rough xr/S ~ 8 lies inside the band.
reattachment_length_xr_over_h.gt_value_source: This repo's calibrated oracle for this case at its own grid level (20800 cells), re-measured under issue #119; T_good = 5% and T_bad = 15% of |gt| per the integral tier. The line this replaces credited an 'ngspice/ccx oracle' and 6%/18% bands — the first was a hard-coded template constant in tools/autocal_kpis.py rather than a fact about this case (fixed, #40), the second never matched the T_good / T_bad actually stored here.

oracle_provenance.method: solution/solve.sh in sim-benchmark-cfd-fullstack (ESI OpenFOAM v2412): blockMesh on the case's own 3-block graded blockMeshDict (20800 cells), then simpleFoam with simulationType=laminar to the fvSolution residualControl (converged at iteration 2664 of endTime 3000, final Ux residual 1.7e-08). wallShearStress is sampled on the downstream floor patch by the controlDict surfaces function object; Cf = -2 tau_x / U_ref^2 with U_ref = 1 m/s, and xr/S is the first negative-to-positive Cf crossing past x/S = 0.5, linearly interpolated between the two straddling face centres and divided by S = 0.0049 m.
oracle_provenance.reanchor_note: Re-measured from the recorded case tree and evaluator at reanchor_commit; the reproductions and grid variants below are the auditable basis for the stored reference.
oracle_provenance.reproductions: Three independent extractions of the same run recipe agree: solve_inner.py's own reattachment.dat gives 8.341731; the track evaluator's clean reproduction (artefacts stripped, Allrun re-run, results.csv read by the submission's extract_reattachment.py, which finds the floor by minimum y rather than by patch name) gives 8.34173129, |error| = 2.9e-07 and score 1.0; a third standalone Allrun gives 8.34173129 again.
oracle_provenance.pass_tol_basis: Integral tier (5%) of docs/acceptance.md, floored by the grid-family spread above: 0.64% across a 4x change in cell count, so T_good is ~8x the spread a mesh choice alone produces.
oracle_provenance.gross_error_tol_basis: 15% of gt — three times T_good; at that distance the reattachment is grossly wrong (under-resolved, wrong nu, or not the laminar steady regime) rather than a near miss.
oracle_provenance.wall_clock: 186 s for solution/solve.sh and 186 s for the evaluator's clean reproduction, at the case's cpus = 2.

stopping.note: Shipped with endTime 3000 against 2664 measured iterations -- converged, by 13%, on one host, the same thin margin `lid_driven_cavity_ghia_re400` carried before #273. The cap is raised to above twice the measured cost so a slower path to the same criterion still converges rather than silently reporting the cap's answer. The run is unchanged either way: re-measured at endTime 6000 it stops at the same 2664 iterations and reports the same reattachment_length_xr_over_h = 8.341731, which is this case's gt_value, so nothing moves.
